feed.title: NPR Topics: Politics
feed.subtitle: Follow NPR Politics for nonpartisan coverage of government, elections, policy debates and voting rights. Plus weekday audio from The NPR Politics Podcast.

entry.title: Judge halts construction of Trump's arch. And, Labor Department to release jobs report
entry.summary: A judge has blocked construction of Trump's arch moments after it won federal approval to proceed. And, the Labor Department is set to release the latest jobs report today, a day after stocks plunged.

entry.title: 'He's got to go': Hakeem Jeffries calls for Hegseth's removal but stops short of impeachment
entry.summary: Speaking with Morning Edition, Hakeem Jeffries discussed ending the Iran war, holding Trump accountable and calls for new Democratic leadership, but offered few specifics on how Democrats would deliver.

entry.title: Dearborn, Michigan, mayor on city's record turnout and the election of Abdul El-Sayed
entry.summary: NPR host Leila Fadel speaks with Abdullah Hammoud, the mayor of Dearborn, Michigan, about why his city turned out in record numbers to elect Abdul El-Sayed to the U.S. Senate.

entry.title: Voters under 30 helped drive Tuesday's blue wave
entry.summary: Young voters played a large role in Democratic wins in this week's midterms. People under 30 voted blue at much higher rates than in 2024.

entry.title: A judge blocks construction of Trump's arch moments after it won federal approval
entry.summary: The Trump administration hoped to begin construction immediately after a federal panel approved its arch late Thursday. But just after midnight, the judge issued an order blocking work for 14 days.

entry.title: These are the races in the House and Senate that haven't been called yet
entry.summary: Democrats are poised to have a strong majority in the upcoming Congress. The final numbers are still being determined. Here's where things stand in the races that are waiting to be called by the AP.

entry.title: Melania Trump touts rare agreement she brokered between Russia and Ukraine
entry.summary: The six-day pause from the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky comes as the administration ramps up efforts to secure an agreement to end the war in Ukraine.

entry.title: How North Carolina Democrats flipped several House seats in historically GOP districts
entry.summary: All of these seats were in districts redrawn in 2023 to favor Republican candidates.

entry.title: What the blue wave looked like in North Carolina
entry.summary: Democrats have flipped five Republican-held congressional seats in North Carolina. The surprising results were just one part of the blue wave in a swing state that President Trump won three times.

entry.title: Newsom announces he will commute sentences of inmates on California's death row
entry.summary: California Gov. Gavin Newsom announced that he's commuting the sentences of all inmates on the state's Death Row. The governor says at 548 people, it's the largest death row in the Western Hemisphere.
